MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Agency,
  Community Development Financing Authority,
  Public Improvement Corporation,
  and Library Board of Trustees*

  April 20, 2009

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Agency, the Community
Development Financing Authority, the Public Improvement Corporation, and the Library Board
of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Pro Tem
MacLean at 5:02 p.m., on April 20, 2009 at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on April 17, 2009, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the
Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Kelley
  Council Member Ledesma
  Council Member Schlicht (arrived at 5:11 p.m.)
  Mayor Pro Tem MacLean
  Mayor Ury (arrived at 5:05 p.m.)

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  Irwin B. Bornstein, Assistant City Manager/Director of Admin. Services
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Ledesma

INVOCATION: Council Member Kelley

RECESS

At the hour of 5:05 p.m., Mayor Pro Tem MacLean declared a recess. The City Council
reconvened at 6:01 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

City Council Minutes  1  April 20, 2009
 CLOSED SESSION

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Recognize Chief of Police Services Lieutenant Steve Bernardi, Upon his Retirement
  From the Orange County Sheriff’s Department

  Mayor Ury presented the Certificate of Commendation and City Tile to Lieutenant Steve
  Bernardi.

P2.  Recognize May 2009 as Water Awareness Month

  Mayor Ury presented proclamations to El Toro, Moulton Niguel, and Santa Margarita
  Water District representatives.

P3.  Community of Character Awards

  Tammy Descoteaux presented Community of Character Awards to members of the "Kids
  Against Trash".

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Larry Gilbert, M.V.: requested that the City get compliance from Mission Hospital for the
expansion-related sales and use taxes as outlined in Development Agreement DA2003-1.

Patricia Powers, M.V.: speaking on behalf of the Friends of Mission Viejo Library, reminded
residents that during the month of April, the library will receive $5 per ton of recyclable material
collected from Mission Viejo residences and businesses. The money will be used to purchase
books for the children’s section of the library. She also invited the City Council Members to
attend one of the upcoming Friends of the Library Board Meetings.

The following discussed development problems in the Mission Ridge neighborhood and
construction activity at 26992 La Paja Lane. The residents requested that the City Council stop
the project and two residents requested an amendment to Municipal Code Section 9.01.050
regarding building coverage and the definition of a structure: Christine Saracino, M.V.; Robert
Saracino, M.V.; Richard Cordova, M.V.; Catherine Jasper, M.V.; Stuart Jasper, M.V.; and J.
Cantarella, M.V.

City Council Minutes  2  April 20, 2009
 In response to the letter received from Mr. and Mrs. Jasper and public testimony, the City
Council directed staff not to commence any changes to the City’s Development Code. Further,
the City Council asked staff to prepare a status report on construction activity at 26992 La Paja
and a directed the City Attorney to prepare a report providing a legal opinion on the issues
outlined tonight.

Frank Lieberman, M.V.: invited residents to the annual street painting and fine arts festival, Fun
With Chalk, on Saturday and Sunday, May 2nd and 3rd from 10:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. at the
Norman P. Murray Community Center.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 3, 6, 8, 9, 10 and 12 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion.

Motion made by Council Member Ledesma, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem MacLean, to approve
the Consent Calendar as described below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said
  titles which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title
  and further reading waived.

2.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the City Council Meeting of April 6, 2009, as presented.

4.  Check Register dated March 27, 2009, in the amount of $904,179.50

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

5.  Check Register dated April 3, 2009, in the amount of $1,837,765.40

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

City Council Minutes  3  April 20, 2009
 7.  Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly Report for February 2009

  Received and filed.

11.  Annual Routine Maintenance Program for the Removal and Replacement of
  Asphalt Pavement and Related Services - Hardy & Harper, Inc.

  Approved Maintenance Contract Amendment No. 2 to the existing contract with Hardy &
  Harper, Inc. to increase the contract in an amount not to exceed $40,000.00.

13.  Annual Routine Fleet Vehicle Repairs and Services for Routine Maintenance
  Repairs Agreement

  (1) Approved First Amendment to the existing contract with MV Service Centers, Inc. for
  the period July 1, 2009, through June 30, 2011, to increase the contract amount by an
  amount not to exceed $98,200.00; and (2) authorized staff to issue a purchase order to
  MV Service Centers, Inc. for the period July 1, 2009, through June 30, 2010, in an
  amount not to exceed $49,100.00.

14.  Annual Routine Janitorial and Related Services at Various Park Sites and Facilities

  (1) Approved the Second Amendment for the Annual Routine Janitorial and Related
  Services at Various Park Sites and Facilities contract to Vocational Visions for the period
  of July 1, 2009, to June 30, 2011, in an amount not to exceed $242,776.00; and (2)
  authorized staff to issue a purchase order to Vocational Visions for the period of July 1,
  2009 through June 30, 2010 in an amount not to exceed $121,388.00.

15.  Reissuance of Variance to Municipal Code Firearm Ordinance No. 97-169

  Authorized staff to reissue the variance to the Casta del Sol Homeowners Association.

16.  Annual Rodent Control Contract - Contract Area 1

  (1) Approved First Amendment to the existing contract with Animal Pest Management
  Services, Inc. for the period July 1, 2009, through June 30, 2010, to increase the contract
  amount by an amount not to exceed $ 86,846.00; and (2) authorized staff to issue a
  purchase order to Animal Pest Management Services, Inc. for the period July 1, 2010,
  through June 30, 2011, in an amount not to exceed $ 43,423.00.

City Council Minutes  4  April 20, 2009
 17.  Annual Rodent Control Contract - Contract Area 2

  (1) Approved First Amendment to the existing contract with RPW Services, Inc. for the
  period July 1, 2009, through June 30, 2011, to increase the contract amount by an amount
  not to exceed $ 46,800.00; and (2) authorized staff to issue a purchase order to RPW
  Services, Inc. for the period July 1, 2009, through June 30, 2010, in an amount not to
  exceed $ 23,400.00.

18.  Traffic Safety/Signal Coordination (CIP 797)-Traffic Controller Purchase

  Authorized issuance of a purchase order to Econolite Control Products, Inc., in an amount
  not to exceed $262,790 for the purchase of traffic signal controllers at 110 intersections.

PUBLIC HEARINGS

OLD BUSINESS

NEW BUSINESS

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

3.  Summary of Fiscal Year 2008 - 2009 Budget Amendments to Date

  Council Member Schlicht stated that after these budget amendments, she believes the
  City will be below its minimum reserves by $4.2 million.

  Motion made by Council Member Ledesma, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem MacLean, to
  receive and file the report.

  Council Member Kelley proposed an amendment to the motion which Council Member
  Ledesma and Mayor Pro Tem MacLean accepted as follows: (1) receive and file the
  report; and (2) authorize staff to transfer the appropriate amount from various reserves to
  the contingency reserve in order to maintain a 15% contingency reserve balance.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

City Council Minutes  5  April 20, 2009
 6.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for February 2009

  Council Member Schlicht asked for clarification on the Investment Portfolio Composition
  pie chart, at the top of page 4 of the staff report.

  Motion was made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Ledesma,
  to receive and file.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

8.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority (MVCDFA)
  Treasurer’s Monthly Report for February 2009

  Council Member Schlicht asked for clarification on the semi-annual commission payment
  to Union Bank, noted on page 3 of the staff report.

  Motion was made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem MacLean, to
  receive and file.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

9.  Draft Annual Action Plan for Fiscal Year 2009-2010 Detailing City’s Proposed Use
  of Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) Funds and Establishing CDBG
  Funding Priorities.

  Council Member Schlicht suggested that the recommendation not be accepted and
  proposed two alternatives.

  Ed Ewart, South County Outreach, Lake Forest: requested that the City Council provide
  CDBG grant funding in the amount of $12,000 as recommended by the Community
  Services Commission.

  Motion was made by Council Member Ledesma, seconded by Mayor Ury, to adopt

City Council Minutes  6  April 20, 2009
   Resolution 09-XX Approving the City’s Annual Action Plan for Fiscal Year 2009-2010
  Detailing City’s Proposed Use of Community Block Grant Funds and Authorizing
  Submission of Such Plans to the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development.

  Council Members Kelley and Schlicht proposed an amendment to the motion and Mayor
  Ury and Council Member Ledesma accepted the amendment as follows: adopt
  Resolution 09-10 Approving the City’s Annual Action Plan for Fiscal Year 2009-2010
  Detailing City’s Proposed Use of Community Block Grant Funds and Authorizing
  Submission of Such Plans to the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development,
  as amended to increase the CDBG Public Services funding for South County Outreach by
  $3,000 for a total of $12,000, and decrease funding for Families Forward by $3,000 for a
  total of $5,000.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

10.  Montanoso Locker Rooms Renovation Project (CIP #500)

  The following expressed opposition to the proposed locker room renovation at
  Montanoso Recreation Center: Neil Lonsinger, M.V.; Mark Dobrilovic, M.V.; Barbara
  Anderson, M.V.

  The following expressed support for the Montanoso Locker Rooms renovation project:
  Dr. Art, M.V.

  Motion was made by Mayor Pro Tem MacLean, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to
  move the previous question. The motion was rescinded by Mayor Pro Tem MacLean.

  Motion was made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem MacLean, to
  set this decision aside for tonight and ask staff to return in 30 days with several options
  for the Council to consider for a more financially frugal project.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

City Council Minutes  7  April 20, 2009
 12.  Playground Renovations (CIP 303) -- Pavion Park Play Area Renovations to
  Universal Design Standards

  Motion was made by Mayor Ury, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to approve the
  project.

  Mayor Pro Tem Maclean proposed an amendment to the motion which Mayor Ury and
  Council Member Kelley accepted as follows: direct staff to return with a report within 30
  days, outlining additional options for the playground renovation project.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, AND COMMITTEE REPORTS

19.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Received the report from Council Member Kelley.

20.  Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Pro Tem MacLean announced that there has not been a recent meeting of the
  Foothill/Eastern TCA and he had nothing to report.

21.  San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Received the report from Council Member Ledesma.

22.  Roundabout Intersections Committee Report

  Council Member Schlicht stated that there has not been a recent meeting of the
  Roundabout Intersections Committee.

STAFF REPORTS

City Manager’s Report

City Council Minutes  8  April 20, 2009
 23.  Mid-Year Budget Review for FY 2008-09

  City Manager Wilberg presented the staff report.

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Administrative Services Irwin Bornstein provided
  an outline of staff’s efforts to reduce expenditures and maintain a balanced budget.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem MacLean, to
  adopt Resolution 2009-11 Amending the FY 2008-09 Budget for Adjustments in Certain
  Revenue and Appropriation Accounts.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

City Manager Wilberg outlined the amount that Mission Viejo expects to receive in grant
funding and American Recovery and Reinvestment Act dollars. Mr. Wilberg identified the
projects that the City will address with these funds.

City Attorney’s Report

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS

24.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as
  presented in the staff report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the
  public record.

Council Member Kelley

25.  Urban Land Institute Study

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem MacLean, to formally
  reject the 2007 Urban Land Institute Orange County Technical Advisory Panel final report for
  proposed mixed use development within the Mission Viejo Village Center are, generally
  located in vicinity of the intersection of Marguerite Parkway and La Paz Road.

City Council Minutes  9  April 20, 2009
   On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

Referring back to the City Manager's Report, Council Member Kelley asked for an update on the
Crown Valley Parkway widening project.

Director of Public Works Mark Chagnon provided an update on the Crown Valley Parkway
widening project, specifically outlining the completion of the paving portion of the project.
Landscaping and art elements will be completed shortly.

Council Member Kelley outlined her attendance at Bunny Days and she thanked the Saddleback
Recreation Department, City staff, and the Mission Viejo Activities Committee for a job well
done. She reminded residents of the following upcoming events: Artes de la Vida on Saturday,
April 25, 2009, from 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. at Oso Viejo Park; Fun With Chalk on May 2 and 3,
2009, from 10:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. at the Community Center; and the Seven Parenting Promises
Workshop on May 5, 2009, at 7:00 p.m. in the City Hall Council Chamber. Council Member
Kelley discussed her attendance at the recent Capistrano Unified School District Safety Expo and
she congratulated the Mission Viejo OCSD and OCFA employees who were recognized at the
event; Lt. Steve Bernardi and Battalion Chief Mark Hawkins. She further praised Mission Viejo
Deputies Gary Lewellyn and Richard Olszynski who received the Medal of Valor from the
Orange County Sheriff’s Department and Deputy Mike Danciulescu who received the Medal of
Lifesaving. She also thanked Mission Viejo residents (who work for OCSD in other cities):
Deputy Rick Hasset, Deputy Steve Hoffman and Deputy Larry Packard who received Medals for
Lifesaving and Investigator Brian Sims who received the Medal of Merit. Council Member
Kelley noted that the “Kids Against Trash” are featured on this month’s Community of Character
poster and the word for the month of April is service. She also congratulated Lt. Bernardi on his
retirement stated that we owe him a debt of gratitude for the many changes and improvements he
brought to our City. Finally, Council Member Kelley attempted to dispel a rumor about her that
is circulating on the blogs. She stated that she has tried to clarify this and present the truth but
the truth has not been represented. Council Member Kelley encouraged anyone with questions
to contact her.

Council Member Ledesma

Council Member Ledesma congratulated Lt. Bernardi upon his retirement and thanked him for
the excellent job he has done for the City of Mission Viejo. He also thanked the Sheriff’s

City Council Minutes  10  April 20, 2009
 Deputies who are so highly motivated and dedicated to our City. Council Member Ledesma
requested that the Mayor close the meeting in memory of Michael Chen.

Council Member Schlicht

Council Member Schlicht read an excerpt from the April 6, 2009, City Council Meeting Minutes.
She expressed concern that there has not been a recent meeting of the Economic Development
Committee, yet the Council Member Kelley is receiving proposals from consultants. Council
Member Kelley noted that she did mention this proposal at the April 6th meeting. She was
approached by a market analysis consultant, after the Council received the Buxton proposal, and
she met with this consultant whose price is half of the Buxton proposal. Council Member Kelley
stated that she is continuing to gather information for formal presentation to the Economic
Development Committee at its next meeting. Mayor Pro Tem MacLean confirmed that there has
not been a meeting of the ad hoc committee. He stated that Council Member Kelley met with the
consultant alone and all five Council Members received the same email proposal from that
consultant. Council Member Schlicht referred to Mayor Ury’s comments regarding due process
and stated that there has not been an applicant on the Casta del Sol golf course housing concept.
She noted that she wants the City to balance the budget by reducing spending, not by moving
money or reducing reserves. She asked when the Council will hold a budget workshop. Director
Bornstein stated that the proposed budget is expected to be delivered to the City Council on June
1, 2009, and staff recommends a budget workshop sometime between June 2 and 12. Council
Member Schlicht discussed her attendance at the recent Tea Party, which was the largest rally in
the City’s history. She announced that more than 500 people signed petitions to send a message
to Sacramento and the crowd was eager to get government to listen to them. Council Member
Schlicht wished everyone a happy spring and expressed her hope that members of the
community will come together and support their neighbors in these tough times.

Mayor Pro Tem MacLean

Mayor Pro Tem MacLean referred to comments this evening about a balanced budget. He noted
that staff did present a balanced budget and the City Council has discussed, at length, what
reserve-level is enough. He stated that it’s an academic argument and one individual’s comfort
level is different than another’s. The City Council defined a target amount of 40% and we have
not only met that level but exceeded it with current reserves at 52%. Mayor Pro Tem MacLean
noted that community activists accepted the 40% target level and he reiterated that the City’s
budget is balanced. He expressed dismay at certain Council Member’s attempts to try to
discredit other Council Members and their actions, going back three and four years. He stated
that those efforts, in fact, have resulted in a number of positive things for Mission Viejo,
including an expanded Community Center, an increase in reserves, and an effort to improve

City Council Minutes  11  April 20, 2009
 traffic congestion. The bottom line is that we are trying to work together with the intent of doing
the best for the community. Mayor Pro Tem MacLean stated that he appreciates the opportunity
to serve and he will continue to listen to his constituents and to work for them.

Mayor Ury

Mayor Ury stated that each Council Member, when they are elected, sets a certain number of
goals. He expressed his disappointment at Council Members who play games of “gotcha” and he
stated that this behavior falls under the realm of embarrassing trivia. Some people have a tough
time realizing that they live in a financially sound community, one of the safest in the nation, and
there is really nothing wrong. He stated that honesty, integrity and professionalism are required
of a Council Member and some people will display those traits while others will not. Mayor Ury
stated that the City had reduced spending and the City Council controls the budget process so he
encourages his colleagues to spend time with staff, understand the issues, and offer additional
ideas for reducing spending. Regarding the Tea Party protest, Mayor Ury stated that he heard it
was a great event, he agrees with the effort, however he did not feel welcome because of the
recall signs being displayed. He reiterated that we live in a very well run city and he wishes the
State and Federal government were run so well. Finally, Mayor Ury discussed his attendance at
the great Bunny Days event and he encouraged residents to come out for Fun With Chalk and
Artes de la Vida.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 9:27 p.m., there being no further business to come before the City Council at this
session, Mayor Ury adjourned the meeting, in memory of Michael Chen, to Monday, May 4,
2009, at 5:00 p.m.

__________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of May 4, 2009

City Council Minutes  12  April 20, 2009
